input: n is a positive integer, edges has E undirected valid endpoint pairs in [0,n-1], and succProb has exactly E finite IEEE-754 binary64 probabilities in [0,1]. Python probabilities are ordinary float (integer 0/1 also allowed); JavaScript probabilities are primitive Number. Self-loops/parallel edges are allowed. start_node and end_node are valid IDs. All collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections. Node fields, where present, are ordinary data fields. Every individual collection length and computed allocation dimension/count fits [0,4294967295]; explicitly stated padded sizes and heap child-index arithmetic must also fit the declared exact numeric domain. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is permitted. Preconditions are not runtime-checked; allocation/resource capacity and actual completion still require qualification. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt; separately declared probabilities are finite primitive Number.
return: Binary64 approximation of the maximum path-success product from start to end, returning one for identical endpoints and zero for disconnected or only zero-product paths. More precisely, the maximized path weight uses left-to-right binary64-rounded multiplication from 1; this is not an exact-real arithmetic promise.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs, edge rows and probabilities remain unchanged. Adjacency lists, best array and heap are private; no mutable alias is returned. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Probabilities/products remain finite in [0,1]; underflow to zero is permitted. Both runtimes must provide ordinary round-to-nearest binary64 multiplication for paired numerical behavior. Multiplication by a [0,1] factor cannot increase the represented weight, enabling maximum-priority Dijkstra. Exact-real optimum/tolerance compliance requires isolated numerical qualification. Integer heap/vertex arithmetic remains safe, with child indices bounded by twice the heap length plus one. All integer inputs and integer intermediates (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain in [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n + E + (E+1)*log(E+2)) time and O(n+E+1) auxiliary space. Every adjacency list is expanded once at its final maximum weight; stale heap entries are discarded. At most O(E+1) improvements/heap entries occur. All heap methods, pair records and doubled undirected adjacency entries are charged. Bounds count ordinary built-in allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop, and stated hash/sort guarantees where relevant.

helpers.name: ProbabilityHeap
helpers.contract: Private binary max-heap of [probability,node] pairs, comparing greater probability first and smaller node ID on ties. push restores parent priority upward; pop removes the highest pair and restores priority downward. pop requires nonempty heap.
helpers.cost: O(log(H+1)) time per push/pop and O(H+1) retained storage for H entries; higher is O(1). Full class and all state are included. The complete definition is 1265 UTF-8 bytes; separator newlines are included in total source bytes.
